title: Flatten sentences into words and optionals into values

blocks.text: `map` turns each element into exactly one result; `flatMap` turns each element into a stream of results and flattens all those streams into one. Splitting sentences with `map` would give a `Stream<String[]>`; `flatMap` gives the words themselves.

items: `words(List<String> sentences)` returns every word of every sentence, in order. Words are separated by one or more ASCII whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, line breaks). A `null` sentence has no words.
`present(List<Optional<String>> values)` returns the values of the optionals that are present, in order.

blocks.text: Every element may turn into zero, one or many results; make sure "zero" really adds nothing.

cases.says: It flattens the sentences into one list of words, and the optionals into their values.
Runs of whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks), and whitespace at either end, produce no empty words.
A null sentence contributes no words instead of throwing NullPointerException.
An empty Optional contributes nothing: flatMap(Optional::stream) keeps only the present values.

origin.section: filter vs map vs flatMap at a Glance

concepts: flatMap turns each element into a stream of zero or more results and flattens them into one stream, where map gives exactly one result each.
flatMap(Optional::stream) keeps only the values of the present optionals.
